newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs off highs but tone bullish.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs off highs but tone bullish.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures were off their highs but remained firm in late Friday trade, supported by weak auto sales data and a sharp drop in Tokyo stocks.
Dealers said SIMEX Euroyen futures were also boosted by large buy orders from a major U.S. investment house in early trade.
"They came in to buy about 1,500 lots at the open. Initially, the market was quite quiet but then it turned bullish," a senior trader at a European futures house said.
He said rumours that influential U.S. financier George Soros was liquidating Tokyo stock futures holdings and buying more JGB futures also underpinned the market.
The 225-share Nikkei average ended down 527.05 at 19,804.38, while its September futures lost 550 points to end at 19,795 on SIMEX.
The lead March Euroyen contract stood at 99.21 at 1115 GMT after trading a 99.17-99.22 range against an IMM close at 99.17.
"Sentiment is still quite bullish. If it goes up further, there might be some stop-loss buy orders," a trader at another European institution said.
He said the contract would face some resistance at 99.23-25.
September JGBs breached the technical 126.55 barrier and shot to a new contract high of 126.76 before settling at 126.72. They previously closed at 126.37.
Eurodollar futures eked out more gains ahead of the release of the U.S. non-farm payrolls report at 1230 GMT.

The consensus forecast in a Reuters survey calls for a non-farm payrolls figure of 193,000 in July versus 217,000 in June, and the overall unemployment rate is expected to edge down 0.1 percentage point to 4.9 percent.
The dealer at the European futures house said a payrolls number above 250,000 could spark a sell-off in U.S. treasuries, while anything below 150,000 would spur buying.
December Eurodollars ended at 94.225 against an IMM close at 94.215 on volume of 8,475 lots.
